newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES leads Russian shares higher, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: UES leads Russian shares higher, seen firm.

text.p: UES jumped five percent on Tuesday, pulling up other leading Russian shares behind it in active trading on news of government plans to reform the national electricity company, traders said.
They predicted the market could firm further tomorrow.
"Today was exactly that situation where one share pulls the others along with it," said Pavel Gronbjerg, head of corporate securities at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The Russian Trading System 23 share index rose to 288.63 on $30.4 million traded -- the closest the market has come in recent weeks to the $40 million considered healthy for the RTS than -- from Monday's closing 282.23.
UES shares closed up 5.5 percent at $0.1995 on about $26 million traded after a previous $0.1890.
First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov on Tuesday named government representatives -- top reformers among them --- to UES's board and said state control over the utility might be tightened.
He also said regional power companies should quickly make new share issues to raise investment capital, and urged UES to prepare a plan to issue long-term securities this year.
Traders said the news overall had a positive effect on UES shares, despite possible short-term negative implications for the company of some announcements.
"The fact is that this is a behemoth that is poorly managed and for the first time people are trying to make it work," said Renaissance Capital trader Viktor Pitaleff.

Head of securities at UCB Dmitry Yevenko said issuing additional shares in regional power companies was not necessarily bad news despite the fact that UES might lose its controlling stakes in the companies as a result.
"It's good that the government seriously intends to regulate electricity," Yevenko said.
Other market leaders followed behind UES, as regional energy company Irkutskenergo edged up to $0.23 from Monday's $0.22 close and LUKoil rose to $13.65 from $13.25 previously.
Traders said recent low levels on the Russian market, and higher prices in European markets also helped move the market up and that the trend would continue for the next few days.
"Major investors will also join in the buying when they realise that now is their last chance to buy," said Creditanstalt-Grant trader Andrei Galperin.
But other traders said the trend might be short-lived.
"I still don't see a market turnaround. This is not a signal to everyone to start buying. Investors are still cautious," said Gronbjerg.
